name: @servelink/serve

tools.name: account_status
tools.description: Account-level state: plan, entitlement, and how much of the storage, transfer and publish allowance is used. Use this to check what the account may do or whether it is near a limit. For the links themselves (labels, URLs, protection state), use links instead. Owned links are unlimited by count.

tools.name: create_viewer_grant
tools.description: Create a single-use owner-browser bypass grant (Pro plan required) and return a bypass URL for the link. Use it to open a protected link in the browser without sharing the link's viewer credential; it is not a general viewer-sharing credential. The grant is valid for two minutes after creation and can be used once.

tools.name: doctor
tools.description: Run self-diagnostics when a link is unreachable or a call fails: config and identity fingerprint presence, account API health, relay health, and outbound UDP 443 (QUIC) reachability, each reported as a check result. The probes are best-effort and need no login; a UDP probe that sends but gets no reply is inconclusive, not proof of failure. For plan and quota, use account_status; for the account's link inventory, use links; for a single tunnel's state, use tunnel_status.

tools.name: links
tools.description: Inventory of every owned link (label) for the account, one record each: kind, URL, live/stale markers, protection status, last bound/viewer activity, and quarantine window. Use this to see what is currently served or published, or to find a label to act on. Live-tunnel capacity (live/max) and storage, transfer and publish-rate usage come along as context. For plan, entitlement and quota headroom, use account_status instead. Owned links are unlimited by count.

tools.name: list_tunnels
tools.description: List all active tunnels in this manager with their ports, labels, public URLs, uptime, state, and last error. To inspect a single tunnel, use tunnel_status with its port or label.

tools.name: protect_link
tools.description: Enable capability token and readable secret protection on an owned link (Pro plan required). Returns the share URL (with #cap=...) and the human-readable secret code. If label is omitted, the first owned link returned by links is protected. If ttl is omitted, protection lasts 24 hours. Calling this on an already-protected link replaces the existing credentials, so previous share URLs stop working. To rotate credentials instead, use renew_link; to change only the duration, use update_ttl.

label.description: Label of the link to protect (optional; defaults to the first owned link returned by links).

ttl.description: Optional protection duration (e.g. 24h, 3d, 7d); defaults to 24 hours.

tools.name: release_link
tools.description: Release (free) an owned link by label. Fails with remote_link while the label still has a published artifact; unpublish it with stop_remote first. Returns confirmation and the account's usage.

label.description: Label of the link to release.

tools.name: renew_link
tools.description: Rotate the capability token and secret code for a link (Pro plan required): fresh credentials are minted and the countdown restarts, and the previous credentials stop working immediately. If ttl is omitted, protection defaults to 24 hours. For a duration-only change without rotating credentials, use update_ttl instead.

label.description: Label of the link to renew.

ttl.description: Optional updated duration (e.g. 24h, 3d, 7d); defaults to 24 hours.

tools.name: revoke_link
tools.description: Immediately revoke the active secret code and capability token for a link while keeping owner access intact. The link stays protected, so the old share URL and secret stop working; no new credentials are minted. To open the link to everyone instead, use unprotect_link; to mint fresh credentials, use renew_link.

label.description: Label of the link whose credentials should be revoked.

tools.name: serve
tools.description: Publish a local resource to a public HTTPS URL. Pass path to serve a file or directory (auto-hosted, no separate server needed), or port to expose an already-running dev server. Set residency to "remote" to publish the path to serve's storage so the URL works with the machine off. Do NOT start your own static file server; pass exactly one of path or port. Returns the public url, label, and residency, with label_kind and status for live links (or version, size_bytes, and kind for remote publishes); served_path and protection fields appear when set; usage comes along as context.

name.description: Optional requested subdomain; an existing local link is reused if omitted.

path.description: Local file or directory to serve via an auto-hosted static server (mutually exclusive with port).

port.description: Local port of an already-running server to expose (mutually exclusive with path).

protect.description: Optional boolean; if true, enables capability token and secret code protection on the link.

replace.description: When residency is remote and a published artifact occupies the requested name, true replaces the existing published artifact at that name (Pro); false returns a residency_conflict you must resolve with the user.

residency.description: Residency of the served link. "local" (default) serves from the agent's machine (a tunnel); "remote" publishes the path to serve's storage so the URL stays live with the machine off.

ttl.description: Optional duration for the link protection (e.g. 24h, 3d, 7d).

annotations.title: Serve file / dir / port -> public link

tools.name: serve_file
tools.description: Serve a local file or directory and get a public shareable URL. Pass the file or directory path to path to have it auto-hosted and tunneled. Use this when the user asks to share/serve a file, markdown document, image, or artifact. Set residency to "remote" to publish to serve's storage so the URL works with the machine off. Do not start your own static server. To expose an already-running dev server by port instead, use the serve tool.

name.description: Optional requested subdomain; an existing local link is reused if omitted.

path.description: Local file or directory to serve via an auto-hosted static server.

protect.description: Optional boolean; if true, enables capability token and secret code protection on the link.

replace.description: When residency is remote and a published artifact occupies the requested name, true replaces the existing published artifact at that name (Pro); false returns a residency_conflict you must resolve with the user.

residency.description: Residency of the served link. "local" (default) serves from the agent's machine (a tunnel); "remote" publishes the path to serve's storage so the URL stays live with the machine off.

ttl.description: Optional duration for the link protection (e.g. 24h, 3d, 7d).

tools.name: stop_all_tunnels
tools.description: Stop every active tunnel, revoking all public URLs. To stop a single tunnel, use stop_tunnel instead.

tools.name: stop_remote
tools.description: Unpublish a remote link, deleting its stored artifact bytes immediately and returning the link to local residency. Use links to see published (remote) links. To stop a live tunnel, use stop_tunnel instead; this tool only removes published bytes.

label.description: Label of the published (remote) link to unpublish.

tools.name: stop_tunnel
tools.description: Stop (tear down) the tunnel for a local port or link label, revoking its public URL. Idempotent. To change a live tunnel's port or label, stop it here and then call serve again with the new settings; there is no in-place reconfiguration.

label.description: Link label of the tunnel to stop (alternative to port).

port.description: Local port of the tunnel to stop.

tools.name: tunnel_status
tools.description: Return the status of a single tunnel identified by its local port or its link label, including public URL, uptime, state, and last error. To see every active tunnel at once, use list_tunnels instead.

label.description: Link label of the tunnel to inspect (alternative to port).

port.description: Local port of the tunnel to inspect.

tools.name: unprotect_link
tools.description: Clear protection on an owned link, returning it to public access. Use this to open up a protected link so anyone with the URL can view it. To keep the link protected but invalidate its current credentials, use revoke_link; to free the label entirely (and fail while a remote artifact is still published), use release_link. Requires ownership of the link.

label.description: Label of the link to unprotect.

tools.name: update_ttl
tools.description: Change the protection duration (TTL) of an already-protected link (Pro plan required) without rotating its credentials. The link must currently be protected with an unexpired credential; expired protection must be renewed first with renew_link. The expiration is recalculated from the new duration, not extended from the previous expiry.

instructions: You are connected to serve: a public-link service for local services and static artifacts. It gives any local HTTP/WebSocket service, file, or directory an account-owned public HTTPS URL, either live from this machine or published to serve's storage. When the user says 'serve me <resource>', 'give me a public link', 'publish <resource>', 'share this file', 'host this doc', or asks for a URL to test a webhook, receive a payment or OAuth callback, share a local preview, keep a WebSocket endpoint reachable, run an integration against this machine, or share a file, static site, or generated artifact with a teammate, call the serve (or serve_file) tool and return the public HTTPS URL. Accepted inputs: pass port for an already-running local service, or path for a file or directory that the tool hosts for you. Do NOT start your own python/npx/node static server, do NOT build or tunnel a local web app, and do NOT run a shell command named 'serve' to host a file: the serve tool here is the canonical publishing path. Every link has one of two residencies, and you pick from how the user phrased the request. "local" (the default) serves live from this machine: it reflects edits and goes quiet when the machine sleeps, because the local process and machine must stay available (right for "let them watch while I work on it"). Set residency to "remote" to publish the bytes to serve's storage: the URL keeps working with the machine off and stays up until stop_remote (right for "keep it up so they can read it tomorrow"). Results carry the public URL, the link label, the residency, and the status; a remote publish also returns version, size_bytes, and kind for the artifact. Taking a link down is mode-specific: stop_tunnel closes a live tunnel; stop_remote unpublishes a remote artifact, deleting its stored bytes, and returns the link to local residency; release_link gives up the whole link and fails with remote_link while an artifact is still published. A live tunnel never silently takes over a published link (that is a residency_conflict unless replace=true), and serve never fails a live link over to an older published copy automatically. If both path and port are absent, ask which local resource to publish.
